events.title: Closest to Jupiter
events.text: It passes 645 000 km from Jupiter and sends back 17 000 new pictures of the planet, its moons and its ring.

events.title: Saturn's orbit
events.text: On its way to Pluto it crosses the orbit of Saturn.

events.title: Closest to Pluto
events.text: It comes within 12 500 km of Pluto and photographs a vast heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice.

events.title: Into orbit round Jupiter
events.text: Word reaches Earth that a 35-minute engine burn has put it into a polar orbit of Jupiter.

events.title: Past Venus again
events.text: It passes Venus a second time, 600 km from the planet.

events.title: Arrival at Saturn
events.text: It arrives at Saturn after a journey of nearly seven years.

events.title: Past the farthest planet
events.text: It crosses the orbit of Neptune, the first human-made object to go beyond the planets.

events.title: The first pictures
events.text: The first full-colour images are shown, a deep field and the edge of the Carina Nebula among them.

events.title: Launch
events.text: Euclid leaves Cape Canaveral on a Falcon 9, bound for the Sun-Earth L2 point.

events.title: Past Mathilde
events.text: It flies past the asteroid Mathilde on the way to Eros.

events.title: The impact
events.text: Its impactor strikes comet Tempel 1 while the spacecraft watches from a distance.

events.title: Earth and Moon flyby
events.text: It makes a close flyby of Earth and the Moon, one of three that aim it at comet Hartley 2.

events.title: Let go
events.text: Galileo releases its atmospheric probe, which has no engine and falls towards Jupiter for five months.

events.title: The last shuttle sets off
events.text: Atlantis launches on STS-135, the final Space Shuttle mission, with supplies and spare parts for the station.

events.title: Discovered
events.text: Roy Tucker, David Tholen and Fabrizio Bernardi find it from Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona.
